desc:
Ecom Swift LLC provides iOS app development in Swift for founders and businesses that need a real, native iPhone and iPad app. We agree the scope in writing, build in SwiftUI, test on real devices and prepare the release inside your own Apple Developer account.

## What does iOS app development in Swift involve?

iOS app development in Swift means writing a native app that runs on iPhone and iPad using Apple's own language and frameworks. SwiftUI describes the screens, Swift holds the logic, and Xcode builds the result that goes to testers through TestFlight and later to the App Store.

The work is more than coding. It covers design of the screens, data storage, sign-in, connections to your server, testing, an app icon, a store listing and the submission itself. Each of those steps can delay a launch if it is left to the end.

## Why a native app is worth building well

A native app can use the phone properly: smooth scrolling, push notifications, Face ID, widgets, the camera, offline storage and purchases through the App Store. Users judge an app within minutes. If it feels slow, looks unlike other iPhone apps or asks for permissions too early, they delete it.

Building on Apple's standard components also makes the app easier to maintain. New iOS releases tend to treat standard controls well, and any developer who knows SwiftUI can pick the code up later.

## How build quality affects your business

For a company, the app is often the main way customers book, order, learn or pay. Each tap that fails, each form that forgets typed text and each unclear label costs you a task that would have been completed.

Good structure matters over time. When data is saved correctly and the code is organized, adding a feature next quarter is a small job. When it is not, every change risks breaking something else, and the cost of the app grows with each release.

## What a well-built iOS app includes

- A clear list of screens and features agreed before coding starts.
- Native SwiftUI screens that follow Apple's Human Interface Guidelines.
- Support for different iPhone sizes, dark mode and larger text sizes.
- Local data storage, or a connection to your backend or API when needed.
- Sign in with Apple or email, where the app has accounts.
- Push notifications, set up with your Apple developer keys.
- A proper app icon, launch screen and App Store listing text.
- In-app purchases or subscriptions, where the app sells digital content.
- Clean source code with notes, handed over to you at the end.

## How we build it

First we turn your idea into a written scope: screens, features and what is left for later. Then we build in small steps and send you TestFlight builds, so you can tap through the real app instead of reading about it.

The Basic package suits a simple app with a few screens and data saved on the device. Standard adds accounts, a backend connection, notifications and listing text. Premium adds purchases, iPad layouts, analytics and launch support. Before submission we test on real devices, check the app against App Review Guidelines and prepare the listing. Apple makes the final decision on approval, and we cannot promise it.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Write down the one problem your app solves for its first users.
- Gather your logo, brand colors and any content before we start.
- Test every TestFlight build and send your notes in one message.
- Decide early which features can wait for a second version.
- Keep the Apple Developer account under your own company name.

**Avoid:**
- Adding new features while the first version is still in testing.
- Copying another app's screens or branding.
- Collecting personal data the app does not need.
- Treating the App Store review as an afterthought.
- Handing the developer account to a third party you cannot contact.

## Who this is for

A small business owner who wants customers to book or order from their phone is a typical buyer. So is a startup founder with a clear idea and no technical team, or a company with a website that now needs a native companion. If you already have designs, we build to them. If you do not, we propose simple screens for you to approve.

## What we need from you

Send a short brief of what the app should do, your branding files and any content, such as text and images. You will need your own Apple Developer account, and we work in it as a team member with a limited role. We never need your passwords.

If a backend is involved, share its documentation or the API details. After you order, we reply with a checklist and a plan for the first TestFlight build, and at handover you receive the full source code.
